title: What an interval is
summary: Any distance between two notes has a size and a name.

steps.title: Interval
steps.body:
The distance between any two notes is called an **interval**. You already know two: the half step and the whole step. Every interval has a name, and you can always work it out by counting half steps.

**Why it matters:** Bands talk in intervals: "go up a 5th", "the harmony sits a few notes above". Intervals are also what the notes a band plays together are built from, so they lead into everything after this unit.

steps.title: Unison
steps.body:
The smallest interval of all is no distance: the same note played twice, or by two people at once. That's a **unison**.

**Why it matters:** When the band plays "in unison", everyone plays the same notes together. It is also where counting starts: 0 half steps.

steps.title: Counting half steps from C
steps.body: Count the half steps from C to any key and you have the size of the interval.

items.prompt: Play C4, then play it again: a unison.
Play C4, then go up 3 half steps.
Play D4, then go up 4 half steps.
Play G4, then go down 5 half steps.

steps.title: Count it
steps.body: Play any two keys and count the half steps between them. The app shows the interval name, so you can check your count.

items.prompt: How many half steps apart are these keys?
How many half steps apart are these keys?
Play F4, then go up 2 half steps.
